name: Professional listing photo benchmarks
description: Summary figures from October's measurements of up to 392 professional interior listing photos (September 2026): camera lean of vertical lines, focal length, the brightness profile, near-white share, wall colour, saturation, fine detail, styling faults and delivered size, each with its sample size and method note as published in the study.
creator: October (october-ai.com)

changelog.change: First release: the study's summary figures (measured September 2026), each with its sample and method note.

fields.name: id
fields.description: A stable id for the figure.

fields.name: count
fields.description: The number of photos behind a share, where the page gives it.

fields.name: sample_size
fields.description: How many photos the figure is measured on; empty where the page does not say.

fields.name: method
fields.description: How it was measured, as the study page describes it.

fields.name: section
fields.description: The section of the study page the figure is published in.

fields.name: as_published
fields.description: The figure exactly as the study page prints it.

rows.statistic: median lean of vertical lines
rows.method: Canny edges and a probabilistic Hough transform; the length-weighted median of the signed deviation of near-vertical lines from vertical. Lean below about 0.4° reads as 0.00°.
rows.section: Finding 1: the verticals are straight, every time
rows.as_published: median lean of the vertical lines was 0.00°

rows.statistic: share of photos leaning more than 1.0°
rows.method: Canny edges and a probabilistic Hough transform; the length-weighted median of the signed deviation of near-vertical lines from vertical. Lean below about 0.4° reads as 0.00°.
rows.section: Finding 1: the verticals are straight, every time

rows.statistic: photos with too few architectural lines to measure
rows.method: Canny edges and a probabilistic Hough transform; the length-weighted median of the signed deviation of near-vertical lines from vertical. Lean below about 0.4° reads as 0.00°.
rows.section: Finding 1: the verticals are straight, every time
